{{Short description|Concept in mathematics}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], given irreducible subvarieties ''V'', ''W'' of a [[projective space]] '''P'''<sup>''n''</sup>, the '''ruled join''' of ''V'' and ''W'' is the union of all lines from ''V'' to ''W'' in '''P'''<sup>2''n''+1</sup>, where ''V'', ''W'' are embedded into '''P'''<sup>2''n''+1</sup> so that the last (resp. first) ''n'' + 1 coordinates on ''V'' (resp. ''W'') vanish.<ref>{{harvnb|Fulton|1998|loc=Example 8.4.5.}}</ref> It is denoted by ''J''(''V'', ''W''). For example, if ''V'' and ''W'' are linear subspaces, then their join is the [[linear span]] of them, the smallest linear subcontaining them.

The join of several subvarieties is defined in a similar way.
